verdicts.proposedText: At C2, each Geo party member shortens the CD by 1.5s (up to 4.5s) — not modeled; the timeline shows the full CD.
verdicts.rationale: Cooldowns are a core modeled quantity and team-composition CD reduction is on the explicit CANNOT list (cooldownReduce is schema-only, parser deferred). A C2+ player running a Geo team sees the burst come off CD up to 4.5s later on the timeline than in game — a visible, rotation-relevant divergence, same class as the kept Raiden C6 CD-reduction caveat. The C2 energy restore (6 per Geo member, cap 18) is deliberately omitted from the proposed text: energy/particle generation is out of scope by constitution.

groundedIn.claim: At C2, each Geo party member reduces the CD by 1.5s, capped at 4.5s, and this is not authored/modelable
groundedIn.quote: C2: each Geo team member reduces Q CD by 1.5s (cap 4.5s) and restores 6 energy (cap 18) on Q cast — not authored; cooldownReduction/energyRestore based on team composition is not modelable in current schema.

groundedIn.claim: The reduction is per party member whose element is Geo, up to 4.5s
groundedIn.quote:
each party member whose Element is Geo will decrease that skill's CD by 1.5s and restore 6 Energy to Arataki Itto.
CD can be decreased by up to 4.5s in this manner.

groundedIn.claim: The reduced cooldown is this burst's own CD (so the caveat belongs on the burst)
groundedIn.quote: Note: description says 'decrease that skill's CD' but the gcsim implementation reduces ActionBurst cooldown (the burst's own CD) — this matches the in-game effect (Q-CD reduction, not E-CD).

rubricRefs: CANNOT model: cooldownReduce effect — schema-only, parser deferred (the canonical implementDelete trap)
Purpose test: timeline visibly diverges on cooldown timing for C2+ Geo teams
Out of scope by constitution: energy generation (energy-restore half dropped)

verdicts.rationale: Both halves fail the purpose test. The ATK SPD ramp is attack-speed, which is out of scope by constitution site-wide — the timeline never scales any hit timing by ATK SPD (even the burst stance's own +10% ATK SPD is unauthored under the same convention), so there is no per-ability divergence to warn about. Additionally the Kesagiri multi-slash combo is not represented as discrete slashes at all (chargeFrames holds the single Saichimonji slash), so a per-slash speed ramp has no rendered surface to diverge from. Interrupt resistance is something users never expect a rotation timeline to model. The remaining curator-note content is process talk (reviewer to decide).

groundedIn.claim: The passive is an ATK SPD ramp on consecutive Kesagiri slashes plus interrupt resistance, with no authored effects
groundedIn.quote: No effects authored. ATK SPD ramp on Kesagiri (CA1/CA2) only, +10% per stack max 30%, only applies during ChargeAttackState (gcsim asc.go a1Update). Resets on Saichi or non-CA action. Schema has no consecutive-slash counter; reviewer to decide whether to model. Interrupt resistance is not modeled.

groundedIn.claim: ATK SPD does not scale timings anywhere in the planner (site-wide convention, not a per-ability gap)
groundedIn.quote: ATK SPD scales hitmarks at runtime per gcsim, but the schema doesn't encode this for the planner.

groundedIn.claim: The Kesagiri slash combo is not representable as discrete slashes, so a per-slash ramp has no rendered surface
groundedIn.quote: Itto's CA is a 4-state combo (Saichi → Left → Right → Final) gated on Superlative Superstrength stacks with prev/cur-slash windup-frame deltas; the schema's single chargeFrames slot cannot represent the combo.

rubricRefs: Out of scope by constitution: hitlag/attack-speed
Purpose test: no visible divergence — nothing on the timeline claims to show slash-by-slash speed
Curator process-talk belongs in _curatorNotes, not user-facing caveats

verdicts.proposedText: Not modeled: the +70% CRIT DMG on Charged Attacks, or the 50% chance for Kesagiri slashes to not consume Superlative Superstrength stacks.
verdicts.rationale: The +70% CRIT DMG on Charged Attacks is a real self-buff the buff-window system exists to display (the curator note confirms it is schema-expressible — a self critDmg buff on charged-attack hits — but the generator never authored it), so a C6 user checking received buffs during Kesagiri finds it silently missing: a buff-expectation omission, which the add criteria name as decision-relevant. This is 'Not modeled' phrasing, not manual-trigger phrasing, because no effect is authored at all. The 50% stack-conservation half is included so the caveat honestly covers the whole constellation; it cannot be modeled (stack economy is not representable).

groundedIn.claim: C6 grants +70% CRIT DMG on Charged Attacks
groundedIn.quote: Arataki Itto's Charged Attacks deal +70% CRIT DMG.

groundedIn.claim: The CRIT DMG buff has no authored effect (expressible but never wired)
groundedIn.quote: schema can express as a self buff with stat=critDmg on chargeAttack hits, but the generator did not author it; reviewer to wire

groundedIn.claim: C6 gives a 50% chance for Kesagiri to not consume Superlative Superstrength stacks
groundedIn.quote: when he uses Arataki Kesagiri, he has a 50% chance to not consume stacks of Superlative Superstrength.
(b) 50% chance to not consume SSS stacks on Kesagiri — SSS economy not modelable, flag only.

rubricRefs: Purpose test: silent omission of a buff expectation (add criteria: buff/heal expectations)
Authored manual triggers are not 'Not modeled' — inverse applies here: nothing authored, so 'Not modeled' is correct
